notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787; this recitative was written for Vienna, 1788). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation: "cavaliere" where the libretto has "cavaliero", "discoprire" as one word where the libretto has "di scoprire", and "Disingannar la voglio" where the libretto has "disingannarla voglio". IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S21) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.

phrases.original: Come mai creder deggio, di sì nero delitto capace un cavaliere!
phrases.translation: How am I to believe a nobleman capable of so dark a crime!
phrases.ipa: ˈko.me ˈmai ˈkre.der ˈded.dʒo di ˈsi ˈne.ro deˈlit.to kaˈpa.tʃe‿un ka.vaˈljɛ.re

phrases.original: Ah, discoprire il vero ogni mezzo si cerchi;
phrases.translation: Ah, to bring the truth to light, let no means be left untried;
phrases.ipa: ˈa di.skoˈpri.re‿il ˈve.ro ˈoɲ.ɲi ˈmɛd.dzo si ˈtʃer.ki

glossGroups.gloss: to bring the truth to light

phrases.original: io sento in petto e di sposo e d'amico il dover che mi parla;
phrases.translation: within me I hear the duty of a bridegroom and a friend speaking to me;
phrases.ipa: jo ˈsɛn.to‿in ˈpɛt.to e di ˈspɔ.zo e daˈmi.ko il doˈver ke mi ˈpar.la

glossGroups.gloss: both as bridegroom and as friend

phrases.translation: I mean to free her from her error, or avenge her!

glossGroups.gloss: I mean to free her from error
